Λ B and 12
Λ C. This model is applied to calculate the CSB energy anomaly in

1. Introduction
In hypernuclear physics, it is important to extract in-
formation on hyperon (Y)-nucleon(N) interaction. His-

teraction by the studies of hypernuclear structures. For

light Λ hypernuclei have been performed [2, 3]. Fur-

cluster system with sufficient numerical accuracy have
been performed [4, 5, 6]. With these theoretical calcu-

dependent forces of ΛN interaction such as spin-spin
term, spin-orbit term, and etc.

3. Results and discussions
Using CSB ΛN interaction, we first examine the
lighter mirror Λ hypernuclei with A = 7 and A = 10,
such as (7
ΛHe, 7
ΛBe) and (10
Λ Be, 10
Λ B), as shown in Fig. 1.
Among these, 7
ΛHe and 7
ΛBe are the lightest p-shell Λ
hypernuclei for the discussions on CSB effect. The 7
ΛBe
was observed by emulsion and the binding energy in the
ground state is 5.16 ± 0.08 MeV [7]. The binding en-
ergy BΛ of 7
ΛHe in the ground state has been measured
4

to be 5.55 ± 0.10 (stat) ± 0.11 (syst) MeV [19] at JLab.
Thus, ∆BΛ = BΛ(7
ΛHe) −BΛ(7
ΛBe) = 0.39 MeV. As
shown in Fig. 1, our calculated ∆BΛ is about 0.37 MeV
by PK1 EDF, which is close to the data of 0.39 MeV
when the ΛN interaction is fitted to reproduce the cen-
troid data of the ∆BΛ for A = 12 mirror Λ hypernuclei.
We also fit the ΛN interaction strengths to reproduce the
binding energy differences across the range of observed
values.
These results are shown by the blue-colored
bars. Our results for A = 7 hypernuclei are consistent
with the data within one σ deviation. Especially, it is
in good agreement with the data if we use PK1 EDF.
For A = 10 mirror hypernuclei, our calculated ∆BΛ is
about 0.2 MeV by both PK1 and TM2 EDFs. As pre-
viously mentioned, there are two interpretations of the
experimental data for A = 10 Λ hypernuclei. One in-
terpretation, based on Refs. [21, 22, 23], yields a value
of 0.22 MeV, which is consistent with our results (see
Fig. 1(a)). The other interpretation, corresponding to
Fig. 1(b), gives a value of -0.04 MeV, which is inconsis-
tent with our findings. Due to these conflicting interpre-
tations, it is challenging to give definitive conclusions
on the CSB effect in A = 10 Λ hypernuclei. Therefore,
further high-resolution experimental data are needed. In
fact, it is already planned to measure the binding energy
of 10
Λ B with improved accuracy in the J-PARC E94 ex-
periment [44].
Next, based on these results, we discuss the ∆BΛ val-
ues for mirror Λ hypernuclei with A = 40 and 48. For
the combination of 40
Λ K and 40
Λ Ca, Fig. 1 shows that
∆BΛ ∼0 without CSB. When CSB interaction is in-
cluded, the calculated ∆BΛ = 0.1 MeV. For 40
Λ K, at
JLab, it is planned to produce this hypernucleus by the
(e, e′K+) reaction using a 40Ca target and measure the
binding energy of the ground state with a resolution
of 100 keV. Meanwhile, it is possible to produce 40
Λ Ca
by the (π+, K+) reaction at J-PARC using a 40Ca target.
